tasks.title: Establish the executable Rust foundation and command dispatch architecture
tasks.details: Replace the help-only bootstrap with a test-first command runtime, domain-oriented module layout, typed errors, and shared execution plumbing that can support the CLI, MCP server, and TUI.
steps: Create the core modules called for by the spec: manifest, lockfile, source, skill, overlay, adapter, planner, materialize, history, telemetry, doctor, mcp, and tui.
Add a dispatcher that maps parsed clap commands to typed handlers instead of stopping at help output.
Define shared error, response, and application-context types so later commands can reuse one execution model.

tasks.title: Implement `skillctl init` workspace bootstrap and repo integration
tasks.details: Create the manifest-free default workspace layout under `.agents/`, including optional local Git exclusions, without mutating unrelated repository files.
steps: Create `.agents/skills/`, `.agents/overlays/`, and a minimal `.agents/skillctl.yaml` with sensible defaults.
Add optional `.git/info/exclude` handling for generated runtime roots as described by the spec.
Return human-readable and JSON summaries describing what was created or skipped.

tasks.title: Implement manifest loading, validation, and serialization for `.agents/skillctl.yaml`
tasks.details: Model the workspace manifest with strong Rust types, explicit defaults, and validation for targets, projection policy, layout, imports, overrides, adapters, and telemetry settings.
steps: Parse the minimal and full manifest shapes described in the spec.
Validate projection policy, projection mode, layout paths, target names, and import definitions.
Support deterministic serialization so manifest output is stable in tests and Git diffs.

tasks.title: Implement lockfile modeling, deterministic IO, and state versioning
tasks.details: Add `.agents/skillctl.lock` support that records exact source identity, revision, hashes, timestamps, and effective-version data with deliberate schema evolution.
steps: Model lock entries for source type, normalized source URL, selected subpath, commit or digest, content hash, overlay hash, and effective version hash.
Read and write the lockfile deterministically so the same inputs produce the same file output.
Define versioning and migration hooks for future manifest, lockfile, and local-state changes.

tasks.title: Implement skill parsing and validation for `SKILL.md` plus vendor-specific metadata passthrough
tasks.details: Parse skills as directories containing `SKILL.md`, validate the open Agent Skills contract, and preserve vendor-specific extensions without mutating them.
steps: Validate that `SKILL.md` exists and that required fields such as name and description are present.
Check name and directory consistency, frontmatter parsing, and invalid path traversal in overlays.
Preserve supported extra metadata such as `agents/openai.yaml` and Claude-specific frontmatter fields.

tasks.title: Implement the adapter registry and target root planner for all supported runtimes
tasks.details: Encode runtime discovery roots, precedence rules, scope support, neutral-root compatibility, and symlink risk for `codex`, `claude-code`, `github-copilot`, `gemini-cli`, `amp`, and `opencode`.
steps: Define typed adapter metadata for workspace and user scopes, discovery roots, precedence behavior, and compatibility notes.
Implement the documented shared-root planning rules for neutral and native projection policies.
Expose planner results in a form that can be reused by sync, doctor, explain, and JSON output.

tasks.title: Implement source detection, normalization, and fetch support for Git, local paths, and archives
tasks.details: Support the install pipeline’s input sources, detect skills in the required directory layouts, and normalize candidates into a stable internal representation.
steps: Detect candidate skills in `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.opencode/skills/`, and repo-root `skills/`.
Fetch or stage sources from Git URLs, local directories, and local archives while capturing immutable revision information.
Normalize detected candidates with source path, displayed name, compatibility hints, and selected subpath.

tasks.title: Implement effective-skill resolution, overlay application, and conflict handling
tasks.details: Resolve canonical local skills, imported skills, and overrides into one effective view per projected name while enforcing the precedence and tie rules in the spec.
steps: Build a resolver that combines manifest inputs, discovered local skills, imports from the lockfile, and overlays.
Apply explicit manifest priority first, then source-class precedence, and treat unresolved ties as errors.
Produce an explainable effective-skill graph that downstream commands can inspect.

tasks.title: Implement copy-first projection materialization and the `sync` command
tasks.details: Materialize effective skills into runtime-visible roots using deterministic copy mode by default, emit provenance metadata, and prune only prior `skillctl` outputs.
steps: Compute physical roots from the planner and materialize generated copies without touching canonical authoring directories.
Write `.skillctl-projection.json` metadata for each generated projection.
Implement stale-projection pruning that only removes directories previously generated by `skillctl`.

tasks.title: Implement the SQLite local state store and history ledger
tasks.details: Create `~/.skillctl/state.db` as the local system of record for installs, projections, modification detection, telemetry consent, pins, rollbacks, and history events.
steps: Design a versioned SQLite schema for install records, projection records, update checks, local modifications, pins, rollbacks, and telemetry settings.
Add a history-writing layer that records installs, updates, projections, detachments, and cleanup operations deterministically.
Expose query APIs that higher-level commands can use for history, explain, update planning, and TUI views.

tasks.title: Implement `skillctl install` end to end for interactive and non-interactive workflows
tasks.details: Support the main install journey from source inspection through selection, lockfile updates, projection, and history recording.
steps: Implement interactive selection that lists detected skills, locations, pinned revisions, and scope choices.
Implement exact-name non-interactive selection using `--name` or an equivalent selector that never guesses.
Pin the installed revision, update the lockfile and state store, run projection, and record the install event.

tasks.title: Implement the overlay model and `skillctl override` workflow
tasks.details: Add shadow-file overlays in `.agents/overlays/<skill-id>/` so imported skills can be customized without breaking upgradeability.
steps: Resolve overlay files by relative path and make them override upstream content in the effective-skill view.
Implement `skillctl override <skill>` to create the minimal editable overlay layout.
Track overlay hashes in the lockfile and state store so update and rollback logic can reason about drift.

tasks.title: Implement `skillctl update` planning, upstream checks, and local modification handling
tasks.details: Compare pinned installs with upstream revisions, detect overlays and unmanaged edits, and propose safe actions rather than overwriting state blindly.
steps: Check upstream sources and compare the installed pinned commit with the latest available revision.
Differentiate managed overlays, unmanaged edits to projected copies, and detached local forks.
Produce an update plan that can apply, defer, skip, or redirect the user into overlay or fork workflows while recording history.

tasks.title: Implement pinning, rollback, and fork or detach workflows
tasks.details: Let users pin revisions, inspect prior effective versions, roll back safely, and detach imported skills into canonical local ownership when needed.
steps: Implement `pin` and `rollback` against exact recorded versions in the lockfile and state database.
Implement `fork` to copy an effective skill into `.agents/skills/` and detach it from upstream updates.
Record every pin, rollback, and detach transition in local history and projection metadata.

tasks.title: Implement the remaining lifecycle and inventory commands
tasks.details: Fill out the day-to-day command surface for managed-skill visibility and maintenance.
steps: Implement `list`, `history`, and `path` using the manifest, lockfile, projections, and local state store.
Implement `enable`, `disable`, and `remove` so effective-skill selection and projections stay consistent.
Implement `clean` to remove only generated state and projections while never deleting canonical skills or overlays implicitly.

tasks.title: Implement `validate`, `doctor`, and `explain` diagnostics
tasks.details: Build diagnostics that explain why a skill is valid, missing, shadowed, stale, detached, or not loading for a target.
steps: Implement core validation for malformed skills, duplicate identities, invalid overlays, and target compatibility issues.
Implement `doctor` checks for shadowing, stale lockfile entries, unmanaged edits, wrong precedence roots, and adapter-specific loading problems.
Implement `explain` to show the active winner, shadowed candidates, physical roots, target visibility, and drift from pinned sources.

tasks.title: Implement opt-in symlink mode with adapter-specific warnings and safeguards
tasks.details: Keep copy mode as the default while supporting explicit symlink projection where the user opts in and the adapter deems it safe enough.
steps: Add projection-mode handling for `copy` and `symlink` in the planner and materializer.
Warn when selected targets are marked `symlink-unstable` and require explicit override behavior.
Report symlink risks consistently in human output, JSON output, and diagnostics.

tasks.title: Implement telemetry consent, settings commands, and public-only event emission
tasks.details: Add the first-run notice, opt-out controls, consent persistence, and event filtering so telemetry is useful without leaking private-source information.
steps: Implement `telemetry status`, `telemetry enable`, and `telemetry disable` backed by the local state store.
Show a clear first-run notice and persist user consent separately from local history so history still works when telemetry is off.
Emit only public-source install and update events and suppress remote telemetry for private or local-only sources.

tasks.title: Implement the bundled `skillctl` management skill at user scope
tasks.details: Ship and manage a built-in `skillctl` skill that helps agents use the CLI and debug missing or stale skills.
steps: Package the bundled skill as a managed built-in asset with explicit versioning.
Install and keep it updated in user scope without conflicting with user-managed skills.
Require explicit user action for removal and surface its state in history and diagnostics.

tasks.title: Normalize global flags, JSON output, exit codes, and non-interactive behavior across the CLI
tasks.details: Make the command surface stable for humans and agents by standardizing `--json`, `--quiet`, `--verbose`, `--no-input`, `--interactive`, `--name`, `--scope`, `--target`, and `--cwd` semantics everywhere.
steps: Define one response envelope that every command and subcommand uses for success, warnings, errors, and data.
Implement the documented exit-code contract, including warning and validation-specific exits and interactive-input-required failures.
Audit every command so interactive features have deterministic non-interactive behavior and machine-readable output.

tasks.title: Implement trust states and security warnings for untrusted or risky skills
tasks.details: Add the trust model needed to identify risky installs, script-bearing skills from untrusted sources, and operations that should be blocked or downgraded.
steps: Model trust state for sources and effective skills so install, update, and doctor can reason about risk.
Warn or block operations involving risky content according to the spec’s trust-gate and exit-code expectations.
Surface trust decisions in diagnostics, JSON responses, and local history.

tasks.title: Implement the MCP server and v1 tool parity
tasks.details: Expose the lifecycle manager to agents through MCP with the same behavior and structured output as the CLI.
steps: Implement `mcp serve` and the v1 tools: `skills_list`, `skills_install`, `skills_remove`, `skills_sync`, `skills_update`, `skills_rollback`, `skills_history`, `skills_explain`, `skills_override_create`, `skills_validate`, `skills_doctor`, and `skills_telemetry_status`.
Reuse the same typed command layer as the CLI so behavior and JSON output stay in lockstep.
Require explicit parameters for destructive actions and avoid hidden mutations outside managed roots.

tasks.title: Implement the terminal UI for inspection, updates, and history
tasks.details: Build the optional TUI around the same state and command model used by the CLI so it adds visibility without adding a second behavior surface.
steps: Show installed versions, update availability, overlays, local modifications, target visibility, and rollback or pin details.
Map every TUI action to an existing CLI command instead of inventing TUI-only behavior.
Keep TUI reads and writes deterministic and safe for concurrent CLI usage.

tasks.title: Build the full test suite, fixture repos, and cross-platform integration matrix
tasks.details: Added fixture-backed integration coverage for the spec matrix across workspace and user scope, reusable fixture repos for source layouts and failure cases, and telemetry source suppression tests.
steps: Add unit tests for manifest parsing, lockfile roundtrips, overlay resolution, conflict resolution, root planning, install candidate detection, history writes, telemetry suppression, and JSON output contracts.

Create fixture repos for canonical local skills, imported skills with overlays, same-name conflicts, monorepos, broken symlink cases, alternate source layouts, update blockers, and private-source installs.
Run integration coverage across OS, mode, scope, and target combinations called out in the spec.

tasks.title: Add CI quality gates and documentation verification
tasks.details: Enforce the engineering discipline in the spec so warnings, formatting drift, missing docs, and broken tests are treated as defects.
steps: Add CI jobs for `cargo fmt --check`, strict `clippy`, `cargo test`, and documentation verification.
Fail CI on warnings and ensure public modules, types, and important functions are covered by Rust docs.
Make the automated checks align with the growing unit and integration test suite.

tasks.title: Package the binary and release a curl-installable distribution path
tasks.details: Turn the Rust binary into a shippable product with versioned releases and an installation flow that matches the product shape in the spec.
steps: Define release artifacts for supported platforms and ensure the binary bundles required built-in assets.
Add a repeatable release workflow that publishes tagged binaries and supports curl-based installation.
Verify release builds preserve deterministic behavior and sane first-run setup.

tasks.title: Write end-user documentation, command help, and troubleshooting guides
tasks.details: Document the model, command surface, and debugging flows so a new user can understand the system quickly and recover from common failures with one command.
steps: Expand the README and command help to explain canonical roots, imports, overlays, projections, history, telemetry, and trust states.
Add examples for install, update, rollback, doctor, explain, MCP usage, and TUI equivalents.
Document how to diagnose missing, stale, shadowed, detached, or conflicting skills across supported runtimes.

tasks.title: Harden public-only telemetry classification so private HTTPS Git remotes stay suppressed
tasks.details: The current visibility heuristic treats any non-local http/https/git remote without embedded credentials as public, which can emit remote telemetry for private GitHub or GitLab repositories. Default remote Git sources to suppressed unless public visibility is proven and add regression coverage for private HTTPS remotes.

tasks.title: Align the curl installer with the published release artifact matrix
tasks.details: scripts/install.sh resolves Linux arm64 installs to aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, but the release workflow only publishes Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64 artifacts. Either ship the missing archive or fail and document the unsupported platform consistently so latest-release installs do not 404.

tasks.title: Update troubleshooting docs to reflect the implemented TUI and MCP server
tasks.details: Replaced the stale troubleshooting placeholder text for `skillctl tui` and `skillctl mcp serve` with the implemented behavior, CLI mappings, MCP handshake guidance, supported protocol versions, and `--json` automation guidance.

tasks.title: Make lifecycle mutations transactional across manifest, lockfile, store, and projection updates
tasks.details: install, pin, rollback, fork, remove, enable, and disable all persist part of their state before later copy, sync, cleanup, or state-store work completes. A later filesystem or materialization failure can leave .agents/skillctl.yaml, .agents/skillctl.lock, stored imports, runtime projections, and SQLite state disagreeing. Rework these flows so they commit atomically or roll back partial mutations, and add failure-path coverage.
steps: Audit the lifecycle commands that currently write manifest or lockfile state before copy, sync, cleanup, or state-store updates.
Introduce a staging, transaction, or rollback strategy that keeps manifest, lockfile, stored imports, projections, and SQLite state consistent when any later step fails.
Add integration tests that inject mid-operation failures and prove the workspace and local state remain recoverable and in sync.

tasks.title: Fix the broken manual-dispatch path in the release workflow
tasks.details: The release workflow advertises workflow_dispatch, but both jobs immediately fail unless GITHUB_REF_TYPE is tag and GITHUB_REF_NAME matches v*. Manual runs from the Actions UI execute on a selected branch or ref, so the current dispatch path is dead. Either remove the manual trigger or accept a release tag input and explicitly check out and validate that tag before publishing.
steps: Decide whether manual releases are supported or whether tag pushes are the only valid entrypoint.
If manual dispatch remains supported, add workflow inputs for the release tag and check out that tagged ref explicitly in the build and publish jobs.
Add workflow or documentation coverage so operators do not trigger a guaranteed-failing manual release run.

tasks.title: Make `skillctl override` transactional across overlay, manifest, lockfile, and state updates
tasks.details: The override workflow still mutates the overlay root, .agents/skillctl.yaml, .agents/skillctl.lock, install state, pin state, and history without the lifecycle transaction wrapper. A later filesystem or state-store failure can leave those layers disagreeing about whether an overlay exists and which effective version is active.
steps: Wrap `skillctl override` in the lifecycle transaction helper and track the overlay root, manifest, lockfile, and state database before mutation.
Make the command roll back partial filesystem and state changes if any later manifest, lockfile, or SQLite write fails.
Add failure-path coverage that injects a mid-operation error and proves the overlay workflow leaves the workspace and local state consistent.

tasks.title: Honor manifest-configured overlay roots in update and inspection flows
tasks.details: `planner::overlay_state` hardcodes `.agents/overlays/<skill>`, so `skillctl update` misses overlays when `layout.overlays_dir` is customized. `tui::overlay_view` carries the same default-path assumption instead of consistently using manifest override data.
steps: Thread manifest-driven overlay path lookup into update planning instead of probing a hardcoded `.agents/overlays/<skill>` path.
Remove the remaining default-overlay-path assumption from TUI overlay inspection so dashboard state matches customized manifest layouts.
Add regression coverage proving update and TUI overlay reporting still work when `layout.overlays_dir` is set to a non-default path.

tasks.title: Enable positive public-source telemetry classification for verified public Git remotes
tasks.details: The telemetry model, CLI copy, README, and spec all describe public-source install and update events, but `classify_git_source_visibility` never returns `public` for any real remote input. That leaves `emitted` permanently false and `public_source` permanently null for real Git installs and updates.
steps: Design a conservative allowlist or proof mechanism that can classify known-public Git remotes as `public` without regressing the existing private-source suppression guarantees.
Wire that positive classification through install and update telemetry reports so real public Git events can set `emitted: true` and include the normalized public source identifier.
Add CLI and unit regression coverage for both positive public Git cases and the existing local or private suppression cases.

tasks.title: Add release-test coverage for the Windows zip packaging path
tasks.details: The published release matrix includes Windows `x86_64` zip artifacts, but `tests/release.rs` is Unix-only and only exercises the tar.gz branch. The `package-release.py` zip path and the release workflow’s Windows artifact shape can regress without any automated coverage.
steps: Refactor the release tests so the packager can be exercised with both tar.gz and zip targets from the same host CI environment.
Add assertions that the Windows archive uses the expected `skillctl.exe` layout and deterministic zip metadata.
Keep the existing Unix installer coverage while extending the suite to catch release-asset regressions before publish time.

tasks.title: Persist projection records and history when `skillctl sync` changes generated roots
tasks.details: Standalone sync rebuilds the filesystem but does not refresh projection_records or append projection/prune history, so list/path/TUI state can stay stale after target or root changes.
steps: Update the standalone sync flow to replace projection records for the affected scope and append projection and prune history from the materialization report it already computes.
Add CLI coverage that changes enabled targets, runs sync, and verifies both the filesystem roots and the SQLite-backed projection state move together.
Keep the sync mutation path transactional so partial failures do not leave generated roots and recorded state diverged.

tasks.title: Bring bundled-skill and clean mutations under lifecycle transactions
tasks.details: Bundled skill bootstrap/enable/remove and standalone clean mutate projection roots and SQLite state without the lifecycle rollback layer, so partial failures can leave the on-disk projections and recorded state out of sync.
steps: Route bundled skill bootstrap, enable, and remove through tracked lifecycle transactions for every touched projection root and the state database.
Wrap clean in the same rollback model or equivalent atomic sequencing before it clears projection records or removes generated roots.
Add failpoint-driven CLI coverage for rollback on bundled and clean mutation failures.

tasks.title: Restore strict clippy compliance so the advertised CI gate passes again
tasks.details: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` currently fails on `src/builtin.rs` with `clippy::collapsible_if`, which means the repository no longer satisfies the strict clippy contract described in the spec and enforced by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Fix the regression and add a small regression check if needed so local and CI lint runs agree.

tasks.title: Make bundled `skillctl` show up correctly in explain, doctor, and TUI diagnostics
tasks.details: After the bundled user-scope skill is bootstrapped, `skillctl --scope user explain skillctl` still reports `status: missing`, `doctor --scope user` reports zero checked skills and no bundled state, and the TUI inherits the same broken explain report. Teach the diagnostics path to treat the built-in install and its projection records as first-class inputs so bundled-skill visibility and drift are reported accurately.

tasks.title: Reconcile the TUI's read-only contract with bundled bootstrap side effects
tasks.details: `skillctl tui` is documented and tested as a read-only dashboard, but on a fresh home it still installs the bundled user-scope skill before rendering because runtime dispatch bootstraps built-ins for every command. Decide whether TUI should remain truly read-only or whether the help and docs should explicitly call out this first-run mutation, then add regression coverage for the chosen behavior.

tasks.title: Make `skillctl update` respect the active pinned Git reference instead of always querying remote HEAD
tasks.details: Review reproduced that after `skillctl pin <skill> feature`, the update planner still runs `git ls-remote <url> HEAD` and compares against the default branch. Preserve or consult the active requested reference when recording installs and pins so update checks follow the intended branch or tag, and add regression coverage for non-default refs.

tasks.title: Add read-only well-known discovery support for the Agent Skills Discovery RFC
tasks.details: Implement a discovery domain for the current Agent Skills Discovery RFC draft so `skillctl` can fetch `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`, validate the declared schema version and entry shape, resolve relative artifact URLs against the index URL, and expose the result through a new `discover` command without mutating local install state.
steps: Add a `discovery` module with typed index and entry models for the RFC's `skill-md` and `archive` artifact types.
Add `skillctl discover <origin-or-index-url>` to the CLI and runtime dispatch with JSON-first output.
Write unit and CLI tests for origin normalization, direct index URLs, relative URL resolution, schema recognition, invalid digests, and invalid skill names.

tasks.title: Implement verified remote artifact fetch and safe staging for discovered skills
tasks.details: Support RFC artifact acquisition by downloading remote `skill-md` and `archive` artifacts, verifying the advertised SHA-256 digest before use, and staging them into a temporary install root that matches the existing install pipeline. Replace shell-based extraction for remote archives with a safer Rust path that rejects traversal, unsafe links, and unreasonable unpack sizes. Unblocked by maintainer 2026-11-07: the discovery round is scheduled. Implementation constraint from the deferral record: route extracted archives through normalized_extraction_root and the direct-skill packaging path.
steps: Add digest verification and typed fetched-artifact models for `skill-md` and `archive` entries.
Stage verified `skill-md` artifacts into a synthetic skill directory and stage archives into a normalized extracted root.
Add safety tests for digest mismatch, empty archives, path traversal, symlink entries, and archive size limits.
tasks.unblock_when: Met. The archive staging is written and routes every extracted archive through normalized_extraction_root, repackaging a bare skill directory through the direct-skill packaging path (src/source.rs stage_discovered_archive). Tests a_bare_remote_skill_archive_uses_the_direct_skill_packaging_path, a_wrapped_single_skill_archive_installs_like_its_unpacked_directory, and a_wrapped_remote_archive_is_unwrapped_by_the_normalized_root pin that behavior, so T044 can leave its deferred state.

tasks.title: Add managed install support for well-known discovered skills
tasks.details:
Teach the install lifecycle to accept a well-known index URL plus skill selector, fetch and stage the selected artifact, and persist it as a normal managed import while preserving the existing manifest, lockfile, resolver, history, and projection model. Introduce a dedicated source kind instead of pretending discovered HTTP artifacts are Git or local archive sources.

Review repair: Wire well-known discovered skills into the install lifecycle (T045)
T045 owns the install lifecycle wiring: a dedicated well-known source kind in manifest and lockfile, exact-name selection against an index, and persisting a staged artifact as a managed import through the existing install transaction. The identical tree installed as a git URL drives all strategies correctly, so the gap is specific to local-path and archive sources. doctor's projection-drift fix also says 'run skillctl sync to refresh generated projections' (src/doctor.rs:1654), which sync will not do for an edited copy.

Acceptance criteria: the default human output of path lists the concrete paths, history lists events with kind, revision, and time, and list shows the managed skills, or the help and README state plainly that these commands require --json for detail and that the summary line is the intended default.
Evidence: 'skillctl path alpha' prints only 'Resolved filesystem paths for alpha.' with no paths; 'skillctl history alpha' prints only 'Showing 39 history entries for alpha.' with no events; 'skillctl list' prints 'Listed 2 managed skills.' The data exists only through --json or the raw JSON dump that --verbose appends (src/skill.rs:832 builds the path summary; the terminal presenter prints summary plus warnings only). spec.md section 21.3 defines history as 'Show local version and modification history for one skill or all managed skills' and the README command table promises paths and event lists. Tests query SQLite directly, so no test covers this output.

Review repair: Human output for path, history, and list is a single summary line with none of the documented detail
Acceptance criteria unchanged from T075: the default human output of path lists concrete paths, history lists events with kind, revision, and time, and list shows managed skills, or help and README state plainly that these commands need --json for detail.
Evidence: Re-verified at HEAD in /tmp/skr/ws1 and /tmp/skr/ws6 with scratch HOMEs: `skillctl path demo-skill` prints only "Resolved filesystem paths for demo-skill.", `skillctl history demo-skill` prints only "Showing 7 history entries for demo-skill.", `skillctl list` prints only "Listed 2 managed skills."; the detail exists only in --json output.

tasks.title: Let a fresh checkout replace a non-restorable import without hand-editing manifest and lockfile
tasks.details:
On a clean clone, 'skillctl --scope workspace remove skillctl' fails with "skill 'skillctl' is not installed" because remove resolves through the state store's install record, which a fresh checkout does not have, and 'skillctl install <source> --name skillctl' refuses with "skill 'skillctl' is already managed by import 'skillctl'" while the manifest entry exists. docs/troubleshooting.md tells users to "reinstall the skill from a portable source such as a Git URL", but that flow is not executable from a fresh checkout. Fix by letting remove (or a new repair command) work from manifest plus lockfile state when no install record exists, or by letting install replace an existing import after explicit confirmation. Add coverage that runs against a lockfile-only checkout.
Evidence: Reproduced in a clone of HEAD 8cf5035 with a scratch HOME: remove exits 3 with "invalid effective skill resolution: skill 'skillctl' is not installed"; install exits 3 with "skill 'skillctl' is already managed by import 'skillctl'"; 'skillctl sync' exits 3 with "enabled import 'skillctl' has no stored source ... must reconstruct it with 'skillctl restore --frozen'". Populating the import cache by hand did not help. The T068 repin therefore had to be written into .agents/skillctl.yaml and .agents/skillctl.lock and then verified with 'skillctl restore --frozen'. Logged as papercut pc_01M6PMSG3CFSFKBYPD6VXVN3CR.

tasks.title: Store only the selected subpath for Git imports so a source tree with symlinks installs
tasks.details:
handle_install (src/source.rs) and apply_import_revision (src/apply.rs) pass the whole staged source root to copy_source_tree, so a Git install copies the entire cloned repository into ~/.skillctl/store/imports, including the .git directory, and aborts with "symlinked install source entries are not supported for stored imports" when the source tree contains a symlink anywhere outside the selected skill. restore --frozen already stores only the locked subpath (src/restore.rs, copy_source_tree(staged_skill_root, target.skill_root)), so the paths disagree. Store only the selected subpath in install and update, and add a regression test that installs from a Git source containing a symlink outside the selected skill.
Evidence: 'skillctl --json install https://github.com/nibzard/skillctl --name skillctl --scope workspace --no-input' in a scratch workspace exits 3 with "install source '<staging-checkout>/.claude/skills/rust-best-practices' is invalid: symlinked install source entries are not supported for stored imports". The remote is reachable (git ls-remote lists HEAD 736fb43) and the selected candidate resolves to .agents/skills/skillctl, but the store copy walks the whole tree. This is why the T068 pin points at assets/bundled/skillctl and was verified through restore rather than install. Logged as papercut pc_01M6PMSM7CKY5YM7NN4MPR97DG.

Review repair: Install from a Git URL still stores the whole source tree, so the documented reinstall for this repository's own skill needs a symlink-free source or T077
Fresh-clone repair for this repository's own import still cannot use `skillctl install https://github.com/nibzard/skillctl --name skillctl` because install copies the whole staged tree into ~/.skillctl/store/imports and aborts on any symlink. Once T077 lands (store only the selected subpath, as restore already does), the replace flow works against this repository's own Git URL with no extra step.
Evidence: 2026-11-05, fresh `git archive HEAD` clone with a scratch HOME and the skillctl import removed: `install https://github.com/nibzard/skillctl --name skillctl --scope workspace` exits 3 with "install source '<staging>/.claude/skills/rust-best-practices' is invalid: symlinked install source entries are not supported for stored imports". `restore --frozen` of the same pinned revision 736fb43a succeeds in the same environment, which matches T077's note that restore stores only the locked subpath. Replacing from a symlink-free Git source works end to end after the T076 fix.

tasks.title: Report a missing pinned Git revision clearly instead of git's checkout usage error
tasks.details:
acquire_git_revision (src/source.rs) reports the raw 'git checkout --detach' usage error when the fetch leaves the pinned object absent, so a wrong or missing revision.resolved surfaces as "locked revision <sha> is unavailable from <url>: fatal: git checkout: --detach does not take a path argument '<sha>'". Distinguish "the source does not serve the pinned revision" from transport failure by checking 'git cat-file -e <rev>' after the fetch and emitting a dedicated error, and cover it with a test.
Evidence: A one-character typo in revision.resolved inside .agents/skillctl.lock made 'skillctl restore --frozen' exit 3 with exactly that message, while the identical file with the corrected sha restored successfully in the same environment. Manual 'git fetch --depth 1 origin <sha>' plus 'git checkout --detach <sha>' outside skillctl worked, which shows the failure was object resolution, not source availability. Logged as papercut pc_01M6PTGYY03J40B0WX6DR6X.

tasks.title: Read commands can fail with `database is locked` while another process commits
tasks.details:
Read commands (`list`, `history`) open the state store without the coordination lock, so they rely on SQLite's own busy handling. rusqlite 0.32.1 sets a 5-second busy timeout by default (inner_connection.rs:119). A direct read against a working install waited up to 1638 ms on an idle machine, and under CPU saturation the writer's commit outlasted the 5-second default and the read failed with `database is locked`. A user running a read command while another process commits can hit the same error. Decide between raising the busy timeout on read connections and enabling WAL mode, with tests; this interacts with the lock-granularity work in T066. Evidence recorded in notes/state-lock-test-timing.md, section Product observations.
Evidence: Reproduced panic in tests/cli/state_recovery.rs install_rows: `install query prepares: SqliteFailure(Error { code: DatabaseBusy, extended_code: 5 }, Some("database is locked"))` under 8 CPU spinners; probe measured a 1638 ms single-read wait on an idle machine against a committing install.

tasks.title: Make the shared-state-lock recovery test deterministic under parallel test load
tasks.details:
tests/cli/state_recovery.rs:270 ('process A must not write while the lock is held') failed once in a loaded parallel 'cargo test --test cli' run on this branch, then passed on three consecutive full-suite runs here and three on the base commit. The test spawns a real child that holds the shared state lock while another install runs with SKILLCTL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=1000; added parallel tests raise scheduling delay. Making the hold deterministic (block on the sentinel before the lock can be released, or raise the in-test lock timeout) would remove the flake. Logged as papercut pc_01M6PP1QQASGK4VQ9JKTCSZW30.
Evidence: Observed 2026-11-05: one failure of tests/cli/state_recovery.rs:270 under full-suite parallel load; same test passed in isolation, in 3/3 later full-suite runs of this branch, and 3/3 full-suite runs of the base commit extracted with 'git archive HEAD'.

tasks.title: The trust gate announces a block that the apply engine ignores, and the documented exit code 4 is unreachable
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: an apply that a trust gate blocks must not mutate installed content; the refusal must use the documented trust-gate exit code 4 (README exit-code table, spec section 21.5) or, if the gate is deliberately advisory, the 'trust gate is blocking' wording, the JSON blocked_actions field, and the documented exit-code contract must be changed to agree; the behavior must be identical over CLI and MCP, with coverage for both.
Evidence: src/error.rs:19 defines ExitStatus::TrustGateBlocked = 4, but grep across src/ and tests/ matches only that definition; nothing constructs it, so exit code 4 can never occur. src/apply.rs contains no reference to trust, and apply_requested (src/planner.rs:317-339) returns true for UpdateAvailable regardless of trust; the gate only rewrites recommended_action and notes at src/planner.rs:950-958. Reproduced with a script-bearing skill installed from a file:// Git source: 'skillctl update delta' exits 2 warning "trust gate is blocking update apply for 'delta' until it is reviewed or forked" with JSON trust.blocked_actions ["apply-update"] and risk_level elevated, then 'skillctl update delta --apply' in the same state prints the same block warning plus "Applied 1 update with the clean strategy", exits 2, and replaces the projected SKILL.md with the upstream revision. The same bypass is reachable over MCP: tools/call skills_update_apply with an empty argument object applies updates for all skills.

tasks.title: Removing or disabling the last import leaves its generated projection in the reused canonical root, and no diagnostic reports it
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: with the default target set (codex, gemini-cli, opencode, whose physical root is the canonical .agents/skills), remove and disable of the last remaining import deletes or prunes that skill's generated copy (docs/user-guide.md:592 states remove deletes generated projections, and spec section 17.3 requires sync to prune stale previously-generated projections); if a stale generated copy is ever left, doctor or validate reports it; explain must not claim a skill is "not currently visible" while a generated copy sits in a root the enabled runtimes read. Add a regression test that uses the default targets and removes the only import.
Evidence: In sync_workspace_with_policy (src/materialize.rs:215-230), when the physical root equals the canonical root the winners are filtered to imports only, and when that list is empty the loop records the root as reused canonical and continues, so materialize_generated_root and prune_stale_projections (src/materialize.rs:1056, 1243) never run. Reproduced in a fresh workspace with default targets: after 'skillctl remove delta', .agents/skills/delta/ including .skillctl-projection.json, SKILL.md, and scripts/ remains; 'skillctl doctor' reports 0 errors 0 warnings; 'skillctl validate' reports 0 skills checked; 'skillctl explain delta' prints "delta is not currently visible." although codex, gemini-cli, and opencode load .agents/skills; 'skillctl sync' reports "No generated projections were required. Reused canonical root: .agents/skills." and leaves the copy; only 'skillctl clean' removes it. The same happens for 'skillctl disable' of the only import. Control cases prove the boundary: with a second import still installed, remove prunes the projection, and with target claude-code (generated root .claude/skills, not the canonical root), remove prunes it, so the gap is specific to the reused canonical root, which is the default configuration.

tasks.title: explain recommends 'skillctl sync' for a drifted generated copy even though sync preserves the copy
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: when a generated copy holds unrecorded edits, explain's repair advice recommends commands that actually resolve the drift (update --apply --strategy overlay or discard, matching doctor's advice), or otherwise names a command that refreshes the copy; covered by a test.
Evidence: After editing .agents/skills/eta/SKILL.md of a Git import, 'skillctl explain eta' prints "0 of 3 target projections verified. Run 'skillctl sync' to materialize or refresh the remaining projections.", but 'skillctl sync' preserves the edited copy, exits 2, and tells the user to run 'skillctl update eta --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard'. T072 corrected the equivalent advice in doctor (which now recommends the update strategies) but the explain presenter still recommends sync.

tasks.title: Troubleshooting documentation lists 12 MCP tools and omits the shipped skills_update_apply tool
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: the documented v1 MCP tool list matches the tool list the server actually exposes, so an agent reading the guide can discover skills_update_apply.
Evidence: tools/list over 'skillctl mcp serve' returns 13 tools including skills_update_apply, and src/cli.rs:408-422 (MCP_AFTER_LONG_HELP) lists all 13; docs/troubleshooting.md line 462 lists only 12 tools and omits skills_update_apply.

tasks.title: Extend the trust gate to applies that repair unmanaged projected-copy edits
tasks.details:
prepare_update_plan (src/planner.rs) calls block_apply_update only when update_available && !local_modification_detected. A Git import with unmanaged projected-copy edits reports outcome 'blocked' with no blocked_actions, so 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay' (or discard) moves the import to the new upstream revision with exit 2. Fix: evaluate the gate whenever update_available is true; the engine then refuses it with no further change.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-05 with a script-bearing skill installed from a file:// Git source: after editing the projected copy and advancing upstream, 'skillctl update delta' reported outcome 'blocked' with trust.blocked_actions absent, then 'skillctl update delta --apply --strategy overlay' exited 2 and recorded applied with the new upstream revision (lockfile revision moved).

tasks.title: Decide and implement the trust-gate scope for pin and rollback
tasks.details:
The gate only models TrustBlockedAction::ApplyUpdate for update applies. 'skillctl pin <skill> <revision>' and 'skillctl rollback <skill> <revision>' move an unreviewed script-bearing import to arbitrary upstream content with no trust warning and exit 0. Whether explicit revision commands should be gated is a policy decision that belongs with the W06 approvals and policy specification.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-05: a script-bearing import pinned to a new upstream commit via 'skillctl pin delta <sha>' exited 0 with warnings [] and the projection showed the new upstream body; rollback back to the previous revision behaved the same way.

Closed by maintainer decision 2026-11-07: gate pin and rollback exactly like update apply. Executed by T135: both commands route through the shared engine trust predicate (exit 4), with skillctl review --approve and skillctl fork <skill> as the recorded escape hatches; acceptance covered in tests/cli/trust_gate.rs.
tasks.unblock_when: T054 specifies the approval and policy model, so the trust-gate scope for explicit revision moves (pin, rollback) is decided; remove looper:deferred and set todo when this condition is met.; remove looper:deferred and set todo when this condition is met.

tasks.title: sync leaves skillctl-generated copies in roots that stopped being planned
tasks.details:
sync prunes only the physical roots the current manifest plans. When the target set changes (for example from codex+gemini-cli+opencode to claude-code), the previously generated copy in .agents/skills is no longer in any planned root, no projection record points at it after rebuild_projection_records_for_scope replaces the scope's records, and doctor's new stale-generated-projection check only scans planned roots. Only 'skillctl clean' removes it. Fixing this needs a deliberate decision about which roots sync may scan (all adapter discovery roots, like clean, versus roots with prior projection records) and tests for scope and symlink mode, so it should not ride along on T082.
Evidence: Fresh workspace, default targets, one local-path import installed, then the manifest targets edited to claude-code only (imports block preserved) and 'skillctl sync' run: output 'Materialized 1 generated projection across 1 root.', .agents/skills/delta/ including .skillctl-projection.json still present afterwards, and 'skillctl doctor' printed 'doctor checked 1 skill: 0 errors, 0 warnings.' on 2026-11-05 with the build from this task.

Review repair: sync leaves skillctl-generated copies in roots that stopped being planned
Acceptance criteria unchanged from T087: changing the manifest target set stops planning a previously generated root, and sync must either prune that root's skillctl-generated copies or report them through doctor; tests cover scope and symlink mode.
Evidence: Re-verified at HEAD 67e4e30 in /tmp/skr/ws4 with scratch HOME=/tmp/skr/home4: after switching manifest targets from the default set (codex, gemini-cli, opencode; physical root .agents/skills) to claude-code only, `skillctl sync` printed "Materialized 1 generated projection across 1 root." exit 0, .agents/skills/demo-skill including .skillctl-projection.json remained, and `skillctl doctor` printed "doctor checked 1 skill: 0 errors, 0 warnings." exit 0.

tasks.title: enable and disable still cannot act on an import a lockfile-only checkout declares
tasks.details:
`toggle_managed_import` (src/skill.rs) resolves through `resolve_installed_skill` and builds its guard from `capture_expected_imports`, which iterates state-store install records. A user who wants to keep the pin but stop projecting an unrestored import still has to remove it or restore it. Reusing `find_manifest_import` plus `capture_expected_import_from_lockfile` and the tolerant projection rebuild would cover it.
Evidence: 2026-11-05, pristine fresh clone of HEAD 18a4ed6 with a scratch HOME and the manifest import intact: `skillctl --scope workspace disable skillctl` and `skillctl --scope workspace enable skillctl` both exit 3 with "invalid effective skill resolution: skill 'skillctl' is not installed", while `skillctl --scope workspace remove skillctl` now succeeds on the same checkout.

tasks.title: Drift repair advice recommends update strategies the trust gate refuses for a gated import
tasks.details:
DriftReason::repair (src/apply.rs:884) always recommends 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard' for an edited generated copy. After T085 those commands exit 4 while an unreviewed script-bearing import has an update waiting, so doctor, sync's preserved-copy report, and materialize's drift reports name commands that are refused. The refusal message itself names the working escape hatch ('--strategy fork'), so no user is stranded, but the advice is no longer truthful for gated imports. Fix by making the dirty-projected-copy advice trust-aware (thread a gate flag to projection_drift_fix in src/doctor.rs:3057 and the preserved-copy paths in src/materialize.rs:750 and src/materialize.rs:1214) and covering it with a test. Related in theme to T083 (explain drift advice), which tracks a different stale recommendation.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06 with a script-bearing skill installed from a file:// Git source, projected copy edited and upstream advanced: 'skillctl doctor' exits 2 and prints "fix: run 'skillctl update delta --apply --strategy overlay' to keep the edits, or 'skillctl update delta --apply --strategy discard' to back them up and drop them", while both commands now refuse with exit code 4 and the message "trust gate is blocking update apply for 'delta'; take local ownership with 'skillctl update delta --apply --strategy fork'".

Review repair: Drift repair advice recommends update strategies the trust gate refuses for a gated import
Acceptance criteria unchanged from T089: doctor's projection-drift fix, sync's preserved-copy report, and materialize's drift reports must be trust-aware so they stop naming `update --apply --strategy overlay|discard` for an import the gate blocks, or name the working fork escape hatch; covered by a test.
Evidence: Re-verified at HEAD in /tmp/skr/ws7 with scratch HOME=/tmp/skr/home7 (script-bearing git import 'gamma', edited projected copy, upstream advanced): `skillctl doctor` exits 2 and prints for each target "fix: run 'skillctl update gamma --apply --strategy overlay' ... or 'skillctl update gamma --apply --strategy discard' ...", while both commands are refused with exit code 4 and the message "trust gate is blocking update apply for 'gamma'; take local ownership with 'skillctl update gamma --apply --strategy fork'".

tasks.title: update --plan writes an empty plan document for a blocked skill and its --plan-file apply is a silent no-op
tasks.details:
apply_requested (src/planner.rs:317) maps a Blocked outcome to a target only for the overlay, discard, and fork strategies, so 'skillctl update <skill> --plan <file>' with the default clean strategy writes a document with zero plans for a blocked skill and exits 0 with no warning; the later 'update --apply --plan-file <file>' applies nothing, skips nothing, and exits 0. This is the silent no-op class T072 fixed for applies. Fix by either contributing blocked skills to a plan document with the gate warning, or exiting 2 with a visible warning naming the strategy that would resolve the edits; cover with a test.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06 with a blocked Git import (edited projected copy, upstream advanced, gated): 'skillctl update delta --plan p2.json' exits 0 and writes a document with plans: 0 and strategy: clean; 'skillctl update delta --apply --plan-file p2.json' then reports ok: true with applied: [] and apply_skipped: [] and exits 0. The equivalent flow with '--strategy overlay' writes a one-plan document and the apply is refused with exit 4 as expected.

Review repair: update --plan writes an empty plan document for a blocked skill and its --plan-file apply is a silent no-op
Acceptance criteria unchanged from T090: a blocked skill contributes a plan entry with the gate warning, or update --plan exits 2 with a visible warning naming a resolving strategy; the later --plan-file apply must not report ok with zero plans and zero skips; covered by a test.
Evidence: Re-verified at HEAD in /tmp/skr/ws7 (blocked git import 'gamma'): `skillctl update gamma --plan /tmp/skr/p9.json` printed "Wrote 0 plans to /tmp/skr/p9.json without changing anything." exit 0 and the document contains plans: [] with strategy clean; `skillctl update gamma --apply --plan-file /tmp/skr/p9.json` reports "Applied 0 updates with the clean strategy, skipped 0." exit 0. The overlay strategy variant writes a one-plan document whose apply is correctly refused with exit 4.

tasks.title: Unscoped `skillctl remove` silently removes the bundled user-scope skill when the name exists in both scopes
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: when a skill name is installed in both user and workspace scope and no --scope is given, remove fails with the same 'exists in multiple scopes; re-run with --scope' resolution error that disable, enable, and override already use, or the chosen precedence is documented and covered by a regression test. The bundled-name collision, which is this repository's own committed configuration (workspace import 'skillctl' plus the bundled user-scope skill), must not silently delete the user-scope bundled skill while leaving the workspace import installed.
Evidence: Fresh clone of HEAD 67e4e30 at /tmp/skr/clone14 with scratch HOME=/tmp/skr/home14 after `skillctl restore --frozen`: `skillctl disable skillctl` exits 3 with "skill 'skillctl' exists in multiple scopes; re-run with --scope", but `skillctl remove skillctl` exits 0 printing "Removed skillctl from user scope." — `skillctl --scope user list` then reports "No managed skills are installed." while .agents/skillctl.yaml still declares the workspace import. Root cause in code: handle_remove (src/skill.rs:552-568) short-circuits to builtin::handle_remove whenever is_bundled_request matches (src/builtin.rs:388-390 treats any unscoped request named 'skillctl' as the bundled skill), bypassing the multiple-scopes error that find_installed_skill raises (src/skill.rs:1072-1081).

tasks.title: `update` classifies a deleted generated projection as unmanaged projected-copy edits and blocks with the wrong advice
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: when a projection directory is absent, the update report names the missing projection and recommends `skillctl sync` (matching explain's per-destination observed_presence=missing state) instead of setting local_modification_detected=true with kind projected-copy, message 'projected runtime copy differs from the recorded effective skill', and recommended_action create-overlay. A regression test covers a git import with an update available whose generated copy was deleted. Distinct from T090 (which tracks the empty plan document for blocked skills) and from T083 (explain advice for edited copies): the root defect here is that absence is misclassified as drift.
Evidence: /tmp/skr/ws13 with scratch HOME=/tmp/skr/home13, git import 'kappa', upstream advanced one commit, then `rm -rf .agents/skills/kappa`: `skillctl --json update kappa` returns outcome "blocked", local_modification_detected true, modifications [{kind: projected-copy, managed: false, path: .agents/skills/kappa, details: 'projected runtime copy differs from the recorded effective skill'}], recommended_action create-overlay, notes 'unmanaged projected-copy edits are blocking an update'. On the same state `skillctl explain kappa` prints "0 of 3 target projections verified. Run 'skillctl sync' to materialize or refresh the remaining projections.", and after `skillctl sync` the next update reports the update available. Code: first_projection_difference (src/planner.rs:1346-1350) returns Some(path) when fs::metadata on the projection root returns NotFound, and detect_projected_copy_modifications (src/planner.rs:1287-1296) reports it as an unmanaged edit.

tasks.title: sync projects overlay content whose digest no longer matches the lockfile pin, silently
tasks.details:
Acceptance: after `skillctl override <skill>` and an overlay edit, `skillctl sync` either refuses to project content the lockfile does not pin (the behavior docs/user-guide.md documents: 'Fails rather than projecting content the lockfile does not pin') or exits 2 with a warning naming `skillctl override <skill>` as the re-pin command, so the README quickstart flow (override -> edit overlay -> sync -> commit) cannot produce a lockfile/overlay pair that makes every teammate's `restore --frozen` fail.
Evidence: Reproduced at HEAD in /tmp/skrv/ov2 (git import 'delta'): `skillctl override delta`, appended one line to .agents/overlays/delta/SKILL.md, then `skillctl sync` printed 'Materialized 1 generated projection across 1 root' and exited 0 with JSON warnings []. The generated copy .agents/skills/delta/SKILL.md contained the overlay text while .agents/skillctl.lock still pinned the pre-edit overlay digest sha256:08d796... (stale). Committing that pair and cloning it (/tmp/skrv/ov-clone) makes `skillctl restore --frozen` fail with exit 3 naming the digest mismatch, and `skillctl sync` in the clone also fails on the missing import cache. `skillctl verify` does report the mismatch with exit 2 and correct advice, but the README quickstart (README.md lines 93-98 and 152-171) never runs verify. Re-running `skillctl override delta` re-pins the current overlay digest, so the silent sync and the missing quickstart step are the gap. docs/user-guide.md line 391 documents the fail-refusal behavior that sync does not implement.

tasks.title: sync is not idempotent: every run rewrites projections, bumps generated_at, and appends history rows
tasks.details:
Acceptance: running `skillctl sync` twice with no changes leaves the working tree byte-identical (spec.md acceptance 25.2.2 'The same repo produces the same projections across fresh runs' and engineering principle 9 'Deterministic behavior by default'), reports that nothing needed materialization, and appends no new projection history events for unchanged roots.
Evidence: In /tmp/skrv/team-repo (git import 'delta', targets codex, gemini-cli, opencode, claude-code): consecutive `skillctl sync` runs with no manifest or content change each printed 'Materialized 2 generated projections across 2 roots', each rewrote .agents/skills/delta/.skillctl-projection.json with a new generated_at timestamp (1793929010 then 1793929035), and each appended four 'projection' history rows (`skillctl history delta` grew 8 -> 12 -> 16 entries). Because the canonical root .agents/skills is committable and reused as a projection root, every sync leaves a timestamp-only dirty diff in a team repository.

tasks.title: The imported-reviewed trust state is unreachable: no command records a review, so the gate's 'until it is reviewed' path does not exist
tasks.details:
Acceptance: spec.md section 20.2 defines three V1 trust states (local-trusted, imported-unreviewed, imported-reviewed) and section 20.3 keeps script-bearing imports elevated 'until reviewed'. Either a documented command records a local review decision for an import and unblocks gated update applies for it, or the gate message, the troubleshooting guidance, and the spec stop presenting review as a path and name only the real options (skip, fork). The local review semantics may be aligned with the W06 policy specification (T054) and the T086 pin/rollback scope decision, but the unreachable state is a present-round gap against spec.md.
Evidence: src/trust.rs line 18 defines TrustState::ImportedReviewed and no code constructs it; the only import constructor is SkillTrust::imported_unreviewed, whose own comment says 'before any explicit review workflow exists' (src/trust.rs line 74). Verified live in /tmp/skrv/ws2 and /tmp/skrv/ws3: a script-bearing git import with an update waiting refuses `update --apply` and `--apply --strategy overlay` with exit 4 and the message 'trust gate is blocking update apply for 'delta' until it is reviewed or forked'; no CLI command or flag records a review (checked the full command list plus `inspect`, `pin`, and update surfaces), so the only exits are `--strategy fork` or `--strategy skip`. docs/troubleshooting.md line 301 lists 'review the imported skill contents' as a typical response with no command to record that review.

tasks.title: Name SKILLCTL_STATE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS when a state read times out
tasks.details:
A read that does exhaust the 60-second busy timeout surfaces the raw SQLite text, for example 'failed to read schema version in local state store ...: database is locked', without naming SKILLCTL_STATE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS or the coordination lock. Mapping busy failures to a dedicated AppError variant with an actionable message would match the pattern already used for lock timeouts (AppError::LocalStateLockTimeout). Not required by T079: the failure itself is fixed and the wait is documented in docs/troubleshooting.md.
Evidence: Reverting the default to five seconds reproduced the message in tests/cli/state_recovery.rs; src/error.rs:245 renders LocalStateQuery without any timeout guidance.

tasks.title: Drift repair advice names update strategies that are no-ops for an up-to-date import
tasks.details:
For an import whose update check reports up-to-date, every drift-repair surface (doctor's projection-drift fix, sync's preserved-copy warning, and now explain's summary) recommends 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard', but both commands are no-ops: they exit 2 with "the requested apply changed nothing; '<skill>' was skipped: check outcome was 'up-to-date', so nothing was applied" and leave the drift in place. Only 'skillctl sync --discard' refreshes the copy in that state. Cause: apply_requested (src/planner.rs:320-336) maps UpdateCheckOutcome::UpToDate to false, so an up-to-date import never becomes an apply target even when its generated copies hold unrecorded edits (the Blocked branch, which does allow the repair strategies, is only reached when an update is available). T072 fixed the equivalent LocalSource branch by keying on local_modification_detected; the UpToDate branch needs the same treatment, or the advice must become state-aware the way T089 proposes for the trust gate. Acceptance criteria: with an up-to-date import and an edited generated copy, at least one advertised repair command resolves the drift (overlay keeps the edits, discard backs them up and drops them), or the advice names the command that does; covered by a test.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06 in a scratch workspace under the session TMPDIR with a file:// Git import 'release-notes' (claude-code target), generated copy edited, no upstream change: 'skillctl explain release-notes' and 'skillctl doctor' both recommend 'update release-notes --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard'; running either prints "Checked 1 managed skill. 0 update available, 0 blocked, 1 up to date ... Applied 0 updates ... skipped 1" plus "warning: the requested apply changed nothing; 'release-notes' was skipped: check outcome was 'up-to-date', so nothing was applied" and exits 2, and explain still reports 0 of 1 target projections verified. After advancing the same source one commit, the check outcome becomes 'blocked' and 'update --apply --strategy overlay' exits 0 and clears the drift (covered by the new test explain_names_a_working_repair_for_an_edited_generated_copy in tests/cli/drift.rs). 'skillctl sync --discard' resolves the up-to-date case (exit 0, explain then reports 1 of 1 verified). Root cause read at src/planner.rs:320-336 (UpToDate => false).

tasks.title: explain diagnoses a deliberately disabled import as a stale lockfile entry
tasks.details:
Acceptance: an import the user disabled with 'skillctl disable' must not be reported as 'stale-lockfile-entry'. The manifest and the lockfile agree; only the disable decision stops a candidate from resolving. The issue must either not fire when the manifest import has enabled: false, or its fix must name 'skillctl enable <skill>' or 'skillctl remove <skill>'. The current fix text, 'remove the stale entry or reinstall the skill', invites hand-editing .agents/skillctl.lock, and docs/troubleshooting.md repeats that advice for this issue code, which would break frozen restore.
Evidence: Isolated workspace, git fixture, fresh HOME: install ai-sdk, run 'skillctl disable ai-sdk', then 'skillctl explain ai-sdk'. Output: 'ai-sdk is not currently visible.', warning "manifest import 'ai-sdk' exists but is disabled; fix: run skillctl enable ai-sdk", and warning "lockfile still contains 'ai-sdk' even though no active candidate resolves for it; fix: remove the stale entry or reinstall the skill". JSON issues are disabled-import and stale-lockfile-entry, exit code 2. Reproduced with the default targets and with claude-code only, with and without a remaining generated copy. Source: missing_skill_issues in src/doctor.rs:2503 emits stale-lockfile-entry whenever lockfile.imports contains the name and no candidate resolves; the disabled-import issue built just above it (src/doctor.rs:2478) shows the enabled flag is available at that point. docs/user-guide.md states disabled imports stay on disk but stop participating in resolution until re-enabled, so the entry is not stale.

tasks.title: --scope user disable refuses the bundled skill with a stale-plan error when a workspace import shares its name
tasks.details:
The lockfile pins imports by id without a scope. In a checkout that bootstraps the bundled user-scope skill while the workspace manifest declares a workspace import under the same name, toggle_managed_import pairs the bundled install record's effective_version_hash with the workspace import's lockfile entry, so the guarded plan always reports a stale plan and disable never runs. Pre-existing at HEAD and unchanged by T088; fixing it needs either a scope-aware lockfile lookup or an explicit name-collision refusal in the toggle. Enable is unaffected because classify_bundled_request routes the bundled request elsewhere.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 with binaries built from HEAD ef6af04 and from this change, run in a lockfile-only checkout of the repository's own .agents with a scratch HOME: both print "plan 'disable-skillctl' is stale: imports.skillctl.hashes.effective_version is 'sha256:e6536fdcc160864a3b1bdde5eeecc581e0ed2db52461029a5566d440efcee33b' but the plan was built against 'sha256:8d49e3be16eb5ab173fe646d713989c09425ff768d3356411b67f26e0146aef3'" and exit 3, for both unscoped and '--scope user disable skillctl'.

tasks.title: `update` does not name a projection destination the manifest plans but no projection record covers
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: when a manifest plans a root that has no projection record for a managed skill (for example after the target set changes and before `skillctl sync` runs), `skillctl --json update <skill>` names that destination in `missing_projections` and recommends `skillctl sync`, matching what `explain` reports as observed_presence=missing for the same root. Today the check is record-driven: detect_projected_copy_modifications (src/planner.rs) classifies only roots that have a ProjectionRecord with a matching effective_version_hash, and its planned-root fallback reports only ProjectionState::Drift, not Absent, so a planned-but-unrecorded root is invisible to update. Closing it needs a decision about the source of truth (manifest plan assignments, as explain uses, versus projection records) and about target labels for roots without records.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 in a scratch workspace: install a git import with the default target set (projection materialized under .agents/skills), then rewrite .agents/skillctl.yaml to `targets:\n  - claude-code` without syncing. `skillctl --json update <skill>` returns outcome up-to-date with no missing_projections and warnings [], while `skillctl --json explain <skill>` returns [("claude-code", "missing")] and `skillctl doctor` reports missing-projection for the same root.

tasks.title: Projection metadata generated_at uses raw unix seconds while every other timestamp is RFC3339
tasks.details:
.skillctl-projection.json stores generated_at as raw unix seconds (materialize::projection_timestamp), while ProjectionRecord.generated_at in the state store must be RFC3339 (state::codec::validate_timestamp). Two formats for one field name forced a test rewrite during T094 and can surprise consumers parsing the metadata. Unify on RFC3339 and keep a read-side tolerance for existing epoch-string metadata so committed projections are not rewritten by a version bump alone.
Evidence: Papercut pc_01M6QVEKTMM6QD1RMNF007F302 (2026-11-06): asserting an RFC3339 value against the projection metadata failed on the first test run because the file stores seconds since the epoch; src/materialize.rs projection_timestamp vs src/source.rs current_timestamp.

tasks.title: Drift advice for a gated up-to-date import stays conservative about repair strategies
tasks.details:
trust::update_apply_is_gated (src/trust.rs:270) does not know whether an upstream revision is waiting. So doctor, sync, and explain advise '--strategy fork' or 'skillctl sync --discard' for an unreviewed script-bearing import even when its check reports up-to-date. The engine now allows overlay and discard in that state, because the repair keeps the pinned revision and the gate holds back only applies that move an import upstream. Every named command works, so this is conservative advice, not a dead end. Fix by making the gate predicate aware of whether a revision move is pending, in the direction T089 set.
Evidence: src/trust.rs:270-303 computes the gate from the install record alone; src/apply.rs repairs_unrecorded_edits and run_update_apply now route an up-to-date repair around ensure_trust_gate_allows; tests/cli/trust_gate.rs gated_drift_advice_does_not_wait_for_an_upstream_check pins the conservative advice and still passes.

tasks.title: skillctl remove cannot clear a lockfile-only entry, so a genuinely stale entry needs install-then-remove
tasks.details:
A lockfile entry with no matching manifest import is reported by doctor and explain as stale-lockfile-entry, but no single command clears it. `skillctl remove <skill>` exits 3 in both reachable states: with no install record it fails with "skill '<skill>' is not installed and no manifest import declares it", and with an install record it fails with "skill '<skill>' is not a managed import in the workspace manifest". `skillctl restore --frozen` also leaves such an entry in place. The only supported repair is the two-step workaround now named in the issue fix text: `skillctl install <source> --name <skill>` to re-declare the import, then `skillctl remove <skill>`. Letting `resolve_managed_import` (src/skill.rs:868) fall back to a lockfile-only entry for `remove` would close the gap, but that touches a guarded mutating command and is out of scope for T099.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 in isolated workspaces with a fresh HOME. Case 1, lockfile entry and no install record: `skillctl remove orphan-skill` -> exit 3, "skill 'orphan-skill' is not installed and no manifest import declares it". Case 2, install record present and the manifest import removed by hand: `skillctl remove orphan-skill` -> exit 3, "skill 'orphan-skill' is not a managed import in the workspace manifest". Both clear cleanly after `skillctl install <source> --name orphan-skill`, after which remove succeeds and the lockfile no longer contains the id. The workaround is now the documented fix in docs/troubleshooting.md and in both stale-lockfile-entry emitters in src/doctor.rs.

tasks.title: override and fork refuse the bundled skill with a stale-plan error in a lockfile-only name collision
tasks.details:
Same root-cause family as T100, in a sibling command. In a lockfile-only checkout whose manifest declares a workspace import named `skillctl` (this repository's own configuration), handle_override and handle_fork (src/overlay.rs) resolve the name to the bundled user-scope install record and call capture_expected_imports, which pairs that record with the workspace import's lockfile entry under the shared `skillctl` key. The resulting guarded plan mixes the workspace pin's hashes with the bundled record's effective-version hash, so MutationPlan::verify_against always rejects it. The fix mirrors the T100 disable gate: classify the bundled request before building a plan (handle_override and handle_fork need the same classify_bundled_request gate handle_remove and handle_enable use) and stop capture_expected_imports from pairing a bundled install record with a same-named import's entry. Acceptance criteria: in a lockfile-only collision checkout, `skillctl override skillctl`, `skillctl --scope user override skillctl`, `skillctl fork skillctl`, and `skillctl --scope user fork skillctl` refuse with an error that names the bundled skill and the supported alternative, never a stale-plan message; `--scope workspace override skillctl` still reaches the declared import; a plain checkout without the collision keeps its current behavior. Regression tests belong next to the existing bundled-name tests in tests/cli/bundled.rs.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 with the binary built from this change (T100 fix included), in a lockfile-only copy of the repository's own .agents/skillctl.yaml and .agents/skillctl.lock with a scratch HOME after one bootstrap command: `skillctl override skillctl` and `skillctl --scope user fork skillctl` both print "plan 'override-skillctl' is stale: imports.skillctl.hashes.effective_version is 'sha256:e6536fdcc160864a3b1bdde5eeecc581e0ed2db52461029a5566d440efcee33b' but the plan was built against 'sha256:8d49e3be16eb5ab173fe646d713989c09425ff768d3356411b67f26e0146aef3'; local state changed after planning, so rebuild the plan with 'skillctl update --plan' before applying it" (fork prints the same text under plan id 'fork-skillctl') and exit 3. `skillctl update --plan` is not a valid repair for either command, so the message is a dead end. `skillctl --scope workspace override skillctl` and the review, pin, and rollback paths are unaffected.

Review repair: override, fork, and enable still guess the bundled skill when a lockfile pin shares its name and the manifest no longer declares it
Additional evidence for the already-tracked T109 root cause, verified 2026-11-06 with the T108 binary. In a lockfile-only checkout of this repository's own .agents where the workspace import was removed by hand so the lockfile pins an undeclared 'skillctl' entry, and the bundled user-scope skill is bootstrapped: 'skillctl override skillctl' exits 3 with a stale-plan error naming imports.skillctl.hashes.effective_version. The dead end T109 describes for the declared-import collision is therefore reachable through an undeclared pin as well, because handle_override and handle_fork still resolve the name to the bundled install record and call capture_expected_imports. Related milder case in the same state: unscoped 'skillctl enable skillctl' exits 0 and enables the bundled user-scope skill while leaving the stale pin, so the classify_bundled_request gate T108 added to handle_remove has no counterpart on the enable path. Remove and disable are covered: unscoped remove refuses with the bundled_name_and_stale_pin_error message, and '--scope workspace remove skillctl' clears the pin.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06 in a scratch workspace under the looper TMPDIR with a fresh HOME: copy of .agents/skillctl.yaml plus .agents/skillctl.lock with the manifest import block removed, one telemetry status run to bootstrap the bundled skill, then 'skillctl override skillctl' -> exit 3 stale-plan error; 'skillctl enable skillctl' -> exit 0 'Enabled skillctl in user scope.' with 'imports:' still present in .agents/skillctl.lock.
