tasks.title: Edit repair scans only planned roots, so advice about an edited copy in a root the plan dropped is a no-op
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: with unrecorded edits inside a generated copy that sits in a root the manifest plan no longer includes, at least one advertised repair command resolves the state, or every surface names a command that works (for example 'skillctl sync --discard'). Today update reports the edit as a projected-copy modification (record-driven loop in detect_projected_copy_modifications, src/planner.rs) and recommends create-overlay, and sync's preserved-copy warning advises 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay', but apply_edit_repair resolves drift through dirty_projection_copies (src/apply.rs:2494) which scans planned_physical_root_paths only, so the copy outside the plan is invisible to the engine. Fixing it needs a decision about which roots an edit repair may scan: every documented root for the scope (the set sync's prune pass uses, see unplanned_documented_root_paths) versus planned roots only, plus tests for scope and symlink mode.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 in a scratch workspace (git import 'notes', default targets, projection at .agents/skills/notes, copy edited, manifest retargeted to claude-code without sync): 'skillctl --json update notes' reported modifications [{kind: projected-copy, path: .agents/skills/notes/SKILL.md}], local_modification_detected true, recommended_action create-overlay, and missing_projections for .claude/skills/notes; 'skillctl update notes --apply --strategy overlay' exited 2 with applied [] and warning "the requested apply changed nothing; 'notes' was skipped: no generated copy of 'notes' still holds unrecorded edits"; 'skillctl sync' then preserved .agents/skills/notes (exit 2) and advised the same overlay command, while 'skillctl explain notes' and 'skillctl doctor' reported only the planned root .claude/skills/notes.

Review repair: Preserved-copy repair advice is a no-op for a disabled import, the same planned-roots gap T112 records
T112 tracks the class where the advised edit repair scans only what the active plan covers. A disabled import is another trigger for it: the install record exists, so trust::drift_repair_commands returns UpdateStrategies and disable/enable/sync advise 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard'. Because the resolver excludes a disabled import, the update check reports local_modification_detected: false with modifications: [], so the apply is skipped and exits 2 with "the requested apply changed nothing; '<skill>' was skipped: check outcome was 'up-to-date', so nothing was applied". Repairing today needs 'skillctl enable <skill>' first, or 'skillctl sync --discard'. T112's acceptance should be extended to cover the disabled-import trigger, or the advice should become disable-aware the way T111 made it install-record-aware.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-06 in scratch workspaces under the session TMPDIR (skrev-t111-disable, skrev-t111-disable3) with the rebuilt binary: install file:// git import 'beta' (claude-code target), edit .claude/skills/beta/SKILL.md, 'skillctl disable beta' exits 2 advising 'update beta --apply --strategy overlay' or '--strategy discard'; 'skillctl --json update beta' reports outcome up-to-date, local_modification_detected false, modifications []; 'skillctl update beta --apply --strategy overlay' exits 2 with applied 0 and "check outcome was 'up-to-date', so nothing was applied"; after 'skillctl enable beta' the identical command exits 0 with "Applied 1 update with the overlay strategy. Preserved 1 local edit."

Review repair: The unverifiable-copy advice still names an update repair the engine cannot see for a copy without a recorded digest
The unverifiable-projected-copy repair text names two commands: 'skillctl sync --discard' (works) and 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy overlay'. tasks.title: The trust gate does not fire when the incoming revision introduces scripts, so update --apply installs unreviewed executable content with no friction
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: an update apply that moves an unreviewed import to a revision whose content adds a top-level scripts/ directory must be gated (exit 4, trust.blocked_actions) or at minimum the update check and the apply must warn that the incoming revision introduces executable content; alternatively spec.md and docs/user-guide.md record that the gate deliberately evaluates only the installed content and the W06 policy task (T054, T086 family) owns the extension. tasks.title: Drift repair advice may name update strategies the incoming-scripts gate refuses

tasks.title: Symlink-mode projections link into the immutable import store, so an ordinary edit corrupts pinned content and the resulting error names a dead-end repair
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: with projection.mode symlink (and allow_unsafe_targets acknowledged), a projected file inside a generated copy must not be writable into ~/.skillctl/store/imports; projections should link to a read-only mirror, or the resolver and drift guard must treat a store that no longer matches the pin after a projection edit as a projection-level event. If store divergence is detected, the error must name a working repair: restore --frozen or reinstall both repair it today, while 'skillctl update <skill>' (the first named repair in the current message) exits 3 with the same mismatch error and must not be listed. The README promise 'Local edits in a generated copy are never silently dropped' and the W05 acceptance 'a direct edit survives an unrelated install or sync unless explicitly discarded' must hold in symlink mode or the documentation must state the symlink-mode limitation. Symlink projection mode also has no user-facing documentation (README, docs/user-guide.md, docs/troubleshooting.md mention it nowhere), so its semantics and this hazard should be documented together. Cover with a regression test that writes through a projected symlink, mirroring tests/cli/drift.rs SymlinkProjectionFixture, which today only replaces the link with a regular file.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 at 146bbbf with the built binary in scratch workspaces (since removed). Shape: after install with 'projection: mode: symlink' and allow_unsafe_targets, .agents/skills/alpha/SKILL.md (and .claude/skills/delta/SKILL.md for a claude-code target) is a symlink pointing directly at ~/.skillctl/store/imports/workspace/<key>/<skill>/.../SKILL.md (src/materialize.rs materializes per-file links). Write-through: 'printf "\n# local note\n" >> .claude/skills/delta/SKILL.md' in a git-import workspace put '# local note' inside the stored import file. Consequences: 'skillctl verify' exits 3 ('import delta does not match the pinned content: canonical bundle digest is sha256:afdd... but the lockfile pins sha256:9512...'), and 'skillctl update delta' exits 3 with 'stored import delta content hash mismatch ... the import store changed after install. Run skillctl update delta to re-pin ... or reinstall the skill' — the first advice reproduces its own error. 'skillctl install <source> --name delta --scope workspace' repairs by re-pinning but silently drops the local note; 'skillctl restore --frozen' repairs from the retained artifact with the lockfile unchanged. Copy-mode control in the same scenario: sync preserves the edit (exit 2, preserved-copy warning) and the store stays byte-identical. Existing symlink drift tests model only an editor that refuses to follow the link (tests/cli/drift.rs replace_projected_link_with_an_edited_file removes the link before writing, comment at line 906), so the write-through path is untested. No backlog task tracks store corruption through symlinked projections: T069 is done and covers link-replacement edits only.

tasks.title: A missing lockfile beside a present manifest fails with no named repair on verify and update
tasks.details:
When .agents/skillctl.yaml exists but .agents/skillctl.lock does not, `skillctl update` exits 1 with "failed to read lockfile '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)" and `skillctl verify` exits 3 with "no readable lockfile at '<path>': failed to read lockfile ... os error 2". Both name the file but no repair. Naming `skillctl init` is only correct for a genuinely new workspace: init writes an empty lockfile, and a team checkout that lost a populated lockfile would then verify 0 of 0 imports and look healthy. The repair wording needs a decision per command (retrieve the committed lockfile in a team checkout, run init for a new workspace), then a test. T140 covered the missing-manifest error only.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 in a workspace holding .agents/skillctl.yaml (targets codex/gemini-cli/opencode) and .agents/skills/bare/SKILL.md but no lockfile: `skillctl verify` exits 3 with "no readable lockfile at '<path>': failed to read lockfile '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)"; `skillctl update` exits 1 with "failed to read lockfile '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)". Neither output names a repair.

Review repair: A missing lockfile beside a present manifest still fails with no named repair on verify and update
Acceptance criteria as tracked: the repair wording is decided per command (retrieve the committed lockfile in a team checkout versus run 'skillctl init' for a new workspace) and pinned by a test, so a lost populated lockfile never looks like a healthy empty one.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 at 174fb07 in a workspace holding .agents/skillctl.yaml and .agents/skills/bare/SKILL.md but no lockfile: 'skillctl verify' exits 3 with "no readable lockfile at '<path>': failed to read lockfile ... os error 2" and 'skillctl update' exits 1 with the same raw read error. Neither output names a repair.

Review repair: pin, rollback, override, and fork also exit 1 with the raw lockfile read error when the manifest survives but the lockfile is gone
T144 tracks the raw lockfile read error for verify and update and asks for a per-command repair-wording decision. Reproduced 2026-11-07 at 174fb07 with the T143 fix in place, in a workspace holding .agents/skillctl.yaml and an installed import but no .agents/skillctl.lock: 'skillctl pin rel main', 'skillctl rollback rel abc', 'skillctl override rel', and 'skillctl fork rel' each exit 1 with "failed to read lockfile '<path>/.agents/skillctl.lock': No such file or directory (os error 2)" and name no repair (the strict WorkspaceLockfile::load_from_workspace read these four commands perform after the required-manifest check). T143 deliberately left this path unchanged so it would not pre-empt T144's decision; whatever wording T144 picks should cover these four commands too.
Evidence: Manual reproduction in a scratch workspace (manifest present, install record present, lockfile removed): pin/rollback/override/fork all exit 1 with the raw 'failed to read lockfile ... os error 2' line. Not covered by a test yet; T144's acceptance criteria call for the wording decision plus a test.

tasks.title: update planning refuses the whole workspace while one import's store diverges from its pin
tasks.details:
Symlink-mode sync now tolerates a store that no longer matches its pin and preserves the projection, but update planning still resolves every import with the Fail policy, so one diverged import blocks updates for all skills. A scoped tolerance (the same StoreDivergencePolicy the drift guard uses) or a named skip would let unrelated skills update while the diverged import stays reported.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 in a scratch symlink-mode workspace with two imports: after a write-through on 'delta', 'skillctl update other --apply' exited 3 with "stored import 'delta' content hash mismatch" while 'skillctl sync' preserved delta's copy and exited 2.

tasks.title: update <diverged skill> --apply --strategy fork still refuses although the fork strategy reads the stored bytes it would keep
tasks.details:
A run that names the diverged skill refuses at planning time with the store-mismatch error regardless of --strategy, so 'skillctl update <skill> --apply --strategy fork' exits 3 even though the fork is the one apply that keeps the edit. The standalone 'skillctl fork <skill>' that every repair text names works and is pinned by tests. Lifting the fork strategy would require the check to run through a diverged baseline; current behavior matches the T142 contract that update never repairs what it resolves through.
Evidence: Verified 2026-11-07 in a scratch symlink-mode workspace after a write-through on 'delta': 'skillctl update delta --apply --strategy fork' exits 3 with the mismatch error, while 'skillctl fork delta' exits 0 and copies the diverged bytes into a canonical skill (tests/cli/drift.rs fork_keeps_a_write_through_edit_before_the_store_is_repaired).

Review repair: update <diverged skill> --apply --strategy fork still refuses on a diverged import store
Acceptance criteria as tracked: either the fork strategy runs through a diverged baseline because it is the one apply that keeps the stored bytes, or the refusal keeps documenting 'skillctl fork <skill>' as the named repair, matching the T142 contract that update never repairs what it resolves through.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 at 174fb07 in a symlink-mode scratch workspace after a write-through edit on a git import: 'skillctl update beta --apply --strategy fork' exits 3 with the stored-import content hash mismatch, and 'skillctl update beta' exits 3 the same way, while 'skillctl sync' preserves the copy and exits 2 and 'skillctl restore --frozen' repairs the store.

tasks.title: A stale plan document applied to a gated import reports the trust gate first, so the repair it names is a dead end
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: applying a stale plan document to a gated import must fail with the stale-plan error (exit 3) or otherwise make the staleness visible, because no review can make an outdated plan applicable; the refusal must never name a repair that cannot make the requested operation succeed. The plan-document gate must also reach parity with the engine predicate: an apply whose proposed revision already equals the installed revision is not a revision move and must not be gated, matching ensure_revision_apply_is_allowed. Cover with a regression test that re-applies a plan after its target revision was already applied and the import returned to imported-unreviewed.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 with the built binary in a scratch workspace (script-bearing git import delta, upstream advanced one commit after install): (1) skillctl update delta --plan-file plan.json --apply exits 0 and applies; (2) re-running the identical command exits 4 with 'trust gate is blocking update apply for delta ... record a local review with skillctl review delta --approve'; (3) after running that exact review, the same command exits 3 with 'plan update-apply-delta is stale: imports.delta.revision.resolved ... but the plan was built against ...'. So the step-2 advice cannot unblock the operation. The step-2 gate also fired although the plan's proposed revision already equaled the installed revision. Code: the gate loop at src/apply.rs:2048-2051 runs before the per-target mutation plan whose stale check produces StalePlan (stale_import at src/apply.rs:479,530), and the plan-document trust at src/planner.rs:1082-1103 (update_apply_gate_trust) is recomputed from install state alone with no revision-move consideration, unlike the engine's own no-move allowance at src/apply.rs:1983-1986. No test in tests/cli/update_apply.rs or tests/cli/drift.rs covers the stale-plus-gated interaction.

tasks.title: doctor stays quiet when a manifest survives but the lockfile is gone and no imports are declared
tasks.details:
When .agents/skillctl.yaml is present, .agents/skillctl.lock is absent, and the manifest declares no imports, `skillctl doctor` exits 0 with '0 errors, 0 warnings' while `verify` and `update` refuse. doctor reports the loss only when the manifest declares imports, through the per-import `missing-lockfile-entry` issue (src/doctor.rs), so the no-imports case is silent. The T123/T126 convention is that doctor agrees with the commands that refuse; a gated `lockfile-missing` warning (gated like `manifest-missing` on `workspace_holds_skillctl_state`, here on the manifest being present) would close the gap. Wording must keep the two-repair decision: retrieve the committed lockfile, or `skillctl init` only when nothing was pinned.
Evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-07 in this worktree after the fix, in a workspace holding .agents/skillctl.yaml (targets codex/gemini-cli/opencode, no imports), .agents/skills/bare/SKILL.md, and no lockfile: `skillctl doctor` exits 0 with 'doctor checked 1 skill: 0 errors, 0 warnings.' while `skillctl verify` exits 3 with the new no-lockfile refusal. In the same state plus one declared import (install, then lockfile removed), doctor exits 3 with "enabled import 'rel' is missing from the lockfile".

tasks.title: Drift advice names update repair strategies that no-op while the import's overlay changed since the recorded state
tasks.details:
Acceptance criteria: the repair advice that doctor, explain, and sync emit must name only commands that act in the observed state. Either the update check classifies and repairs unmanaged edits inside a generated copy while a managed overlay changed since the recorded state (overlay edited but not re-pinned, or an overlay directory left unpinned by remove-then-reinstall), or the check's skip reason and every advice text must name the working repair: re-pin with 'skillctl override <skill>' first, then the strategy apply, or 'skillctl sync --discard'. The human output of 'skillctl update <skill>' should also surface the overlay-drift state it records in JSON notes.
Evidence: Reproduced at 8227ca9 through the documented flow (README 'Customize without forking the whole source'): install helper from a git file URL, 'skillctl override helper' pins the overlay, append a line to .agents/overlays/helper/SKILL.md (the documented intermediate state before the second override re-pins), append a line to the generated copy .agents/skills/helper/SKILL.md. 'skillctl doctor' exits 2 advising "fix: run 'skillctl update helper --apply --strategy overlay' ... or 'skillctl update helper --apply --strategy discard'", and explain names the same commands. Both applies exit 2 with "warning: the requested apply changed nothing; 'helper' was skipped: check outcome was 'up-to-date', so nothing was applied" and the copy keeps its edit. The check JSON reports local_modification_detected: false with notes "managed overlay changed since the last recorded install state" and "projection copies may be stale because the managed overlay changed". Mechanism: audit_generated_copies (src/planner.rs:2016) returns early at src/planner.rs:2025 when overlay_state.changed_since_recorded_state, so the UpToDate branch of apply_requested (src/planner.rs:435-447) never sees the edits. After 'skillctl override helper' re-pins the overlay, the same check reports local_modification_detected: true and the same 'update --apply --strategy overlay' repairs the copy, so a working repair exists but no advice names it. Not tracked in the backlog: no task mentions the overlay-changed short-circuit or its interaction with copy-edit repair (T089/T098/T111/T112/T130 cover the gate, no-op-strategy, removed-import, dropped-root, and incoming-scripts cases).
